The appellate court will likely reverse, so the answer is B. Zoning compliance does not bar a private-nuisance claim, and siting a house to cut off all sunlight to an established solar home, when another placement would avoid the harm, is an unreasonable interference with the owner’s use and enjoyment. Substantive due process is not the theory, and these facts support neither a zoning-violation prerequisite nor a balance favoring the neighbor.

CONFIDENCE: 82
